subject: Pilot ask: no-model-learning for field trial + evidence & transfer options
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@atlasretail.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot ask: no-model-learning commitment and data controls

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Atlas thought the latency/cost profile looked promising for our kiosk pilot. Before we start ingesting live customer interactions we need to confirm a few privacy commitments so Legal and Security can greenlight the trial: 

- A firm "no model training / no model improvement" commitment for the pilot window (we expect 8 weeks).
- Clear ownership and exportability for prompts and generated responses (we need proof we can extract transcripts and derived outputs).
- Acceptable evidence options: nightly SFTP of transcript bundles, or an audit log + per-request metadata feed.
- Retention defaults and ability to route pilot data to an EU-only bucket if needed.

Can you send a short mutual action plan and say what evidence you can provide that shows data was not used for model training? Also loop in your security contact if needed. Legal contact here is legal@atlasretail.com.

Best,
Elena
Director, Product Operations
AtlasRetail

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@atlasretail.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: no-model-learning commitment and data controls

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to support a constrained pilot with documented no-learning commitments. High level: 

- No-Model-Learn toggle: we can enable a customer-level "no_training" flag so requests for the Atlas pilot are segmented and not included in any model improvement pipelines.
- Evidence options: we can provide (A) nightly SFTP export of transcripts + metadata, (B) daily immutable audit manifests that show request IDs with retention tags, or (C) a combined drive/SFTP package plus an engineer-signed statement of non-ingestion for the pilot period.
- Ownership: prompts and responses produced by the service during the pilot will be exportable via SFTP or API; we'll include sample curl and SFTP instructions in the MAP.
- Data residency: we can pin pilot data to a US or EU bucket depending on your preference for the POC.

I'm attaching a short POC checklist and a draft mutual action plan (attached: POC-NoTrain-Checklist.pdf). Can we propose a 90-day retention default for the pilot with the option for Atlas to request accelerated deletion on demand? If legal prefers otherwise we can map that in the MAP.

Next steps: if legal@atlasretail.com can confirm an authorized signatory I will loop in Security (Connor O'Brien) and Product Compliance (Neha) to scope the evidence artifacts and exact contract language.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-04T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Atlas pilot no-train ask — evidence and ops questions (internal)

Confidential — internal thread. Forwarding the Atlas request. Key asks from customer: no_training toggle for pilot, nightly SFTP export of transcripts + metadata, explicit exportability of prompts/responses, and regional pinning.

Questions for Security/Compliance: 
1) Neha — operationally, can we provide an engineer-signed non-ingestion statement covering an 8-week pilot? What artifacts would you include (audit manifest, S3/SFTP filenames, hash lists)?
2) Marissa — for sales/legal cadence: is 90-day retention acceptable as a default? If Atlas requests deletions earlier, what's the SLA to purge ephemeral KV and caches?
3) Connor — for the SFTP option, do we have an existing template for a one-way nightly push (scp/rsync) and do we need a transient service account? Also confirm whether our audit logs include a per-request "learned=false" flag when the toggle is set.

I'm aiming to respond to Elena and legal with a concrete MAP and attachments by tomorrow EOD. Add any redlines you think we should avoid committing to (e.g., absolute guarantees around absence of derivatives across internal analytics).

Rafael

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@atlasretail.com>, AtlasRetail Legal <legal@atlasretail.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-05T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: no-model-learning commitment and data controls

Elena / Atlas legal — appreciate the clarity and the quick turnaround. Per our internal alignments, here is what Redwood can commit to for the 8-week kiosk pilot (summary + attachments):

Commitments (pilot scope):
- No-Model-Learn: Redwood will enable a customer-scoped "no_training" mode that prevents pilot requests from entering any model improvement or training data stores for the duration of the pilot (2026-08-10 to 2026-10-05).
- Exportability: All prompts and generated responses will be exportable via nightly SFTP bundle or via API export. We will include per-request metadata (timestamp, request_id, model_variant, route) in the bundle.
- Evidence: Redwood will provide one of the following evidence packages at Atlas' choice: 
  a) Nightly SFTP bundle (transcripts + metadata) plus a daily audit manifest; or
  b) Daily audit manifest + weekly engineer-signed non-ingestion attestation PDF.
- Retention & deletion: Default retention for pilot data will be 90 days. Atlas can request expedited deletion; Redwood will confirm deletion of ephemeral KV, caches, and S3 objects within 48 hours of a validated deletion request.
- Residency: Redwood will route pilot data to an EU-hosted bucket on request for the pilot period.

Limitations & notes:
- The "no_training" toggle prevents inclusion in our training pipelines but cannot absolutely prevent all downstream internal analytics unrelated to model training (we will supply a manifest of data products that may access metadata; those are governed by our internal DPA terms).
- For the SFTP flow, we will provision a dedicated one-way push to an Atlas-maintained SFTP endpoint or to an Atlas SSH key held in our transfer user. Credentials are rotated per pilot.

Attachments: Atlas_POC_Mutual_Action_Plan.docx (MAP with milestones); POC-NoTrain-Checklist.pdf (ops checklist); Atlas_Evidence_Playbook.pdf (examples of manifests and attestation language).

If this matches Atlas' needs, legal can incorporate the pilot commitments as an addendum (we can propose a short addendum template). Suggested next steps: 
1) Confirm which evidence package you prefer (SFTP nightly bundle vs manifest + attestation).
2) Confirm residency preference (US vs EU).
3) Legal designate to sign the MAP and share any contract clauses you require for the addendum.

Connor (cc) will start a quick runbook for the SFTP transfer if you pick that path. Neha will draft the short attestation language if needed.

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call tomorrow morning to finalize.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0190
